chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak said:
I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'What is the ruling regarding the Zakat al-Fitr for a needy man?' He said: 'There is no Fitrah upon him.'

key_terms.زَكَاةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the alms-tax of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: Is a needy person exempt from paying Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the exemption of the 'muhtaj' (needy person) from Zakat al-Fitr highlights the principle that the obligation falls upon those with surplus wealth, aligning with the juristic definition of nisab. This ruling underscores the social welfare aspect of Fitrah, ensuring that the poor are not burdened with giving when they themselves require support, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding the distribution of alms.
